items.headline: Microsoft launches Scout, an always-on work agent built on OpenClaw and wired into Microsoft 365
items.diff_narrative: Not present on June 3. Microsoft used its Build keynote to introduce Scout, an always-on personal agent it frames as its first "Autopilot," and the project-relevant detail is what it runs on: OpenClaw, one of the three open coding/agent harnesses this brief tracks, is now the engine inside a first-party Microsoft product placed directly inside Teams and Outlook. June 3's coverage touched Build only as the closing day of a conference window and centered its agent reporting on Snowflake's Builder Keynote and Unsloth Studio's MCP build; Scout itself, the OpenClaw foundation, the governed Entra-identity wrapping, and the Frontier-gated private preview are all new today.

items.headline: Nvidia posts Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B open weights, the most capable US open-weights model so far
items.diff_narrative: Not a bullet on June 3 - the Ultra weights Jensen Huang previewed at Computex on June 1 only went live on Hugging Face today, so this is the actual ship rather than a preview. The NVIDIA Nemotron v3 collection now lists the 550B Ultra in three freshly uploaded variants (instruction-tuned BF16, Base-BF16, and an NVFP4 quantized build) plus a reward model. The model scores 48 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, the strongest US open-weights model to date, though it still trails China's Kimi K2.6 at 54, so the "best open model" claim holds only within the US field. None of this appeared in yesterday's report.

items.headline: Microsoft's Surface RTX Spark Dev Box puts the RTX Spark superchip on the desk and ships with Foundry Local
items.diff_narrative: New today. The RTX Spark superchip itself was the June 1 GTC Taipei story, but the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box - Microsoft turning that Grace-Blackwell part into a deskside developer workstation announced at Build - and the on-device Foundry Local runtime that ships with it were not June 3 bullets. The box pairs a Blackwell RTX GPU with a Grace CPU and 128 GB unified memory for up to 1 petaflop, ships as a Secured-core Windows 11 Pro PC with WSL 2 GPU passthrough, and bundles Foundry Local (distinct from the Azure AI Foundry cloud marketplace), whose late-May 1.1/1.2 updates added Nemotron-ASR live transcription, on-device embeddings, Qwen 3.5 Vision, a WebGPU provider, and Linux ARM64 support.

items.headline: SpaceX fixes its IPO at $135 a share before the roadshow, a $1.77T listing
items.diff_narrative: Not present on June 3. SpaceX set a fixed $135-per-share price ahead of its investor roadshow - unusual, since most issuers leave the number open until marketing finishes - in what would be the largest IPO in US history, selling about 555.5 million shares to raise roughly $75 billion at a valuation near $1.77 trillion, targeting Nasdaq under SPCX with pricing expected June 11. The bullet also folds in the AI-lab listing queue: Anthropic's confidential draft S-1 filing after a May round valued it at $965 billion, and OpenAI reportedly preparing its own filing. Yesterday's market story was Broadcom's Q2 AI-silicon print, a different thread entirely.

items.headline: Bay Area June-July events: with Build and Snowflake Summit wrapped, WWDC, Databricks, and the AI Engineer World's Fair are next
items.diff_narrative: Rolled forward from June 3's events bullet. The change is that both anchors of the early-June run have now closed rather than being mid-show: Microsoft Build (Fort Mason, June 2-3) and Snowflake Summit 26 (Moscone, June 1-4) have both ended, where yesterday Build was on its final day and Snowflake's Builder Keynote was happening that morning. The still-upcoming calendar carries forward unchanged in its facts - Apple WWDC26 (June 8-12, keynote Monday June 8 10:00 AM PT), Databricks Data + AI Summit (June 15-18), the AI Engineer World's Fair (Day 0 Sunday June 28, main program June 29-July 2), AI Tinkerers SF meetups, GitHub Universe (Fort Mason October 28-29), and AWS re:Invent (Las Vegas November 30-December 4, registration opening June 16).
